name: Concept I: Laser sail (Starshot-class) — 0.2c flyby
summary: Beyond-target · gram-scale, not a 1 kg probe. Laser-launched 0.2c flyby of Proxima in ~21.2 yr; no destination braking.
feasibility: Proposed Starshot-class architecture; a roughly 100 GW phased array accelerates a gram chip on a meter-scale sail. This is not demonstrated hardware.
showstopper: Kilometre-scale beam control, sail heat and stability, dust survival and the return data link; no chip-sized brake at 0.2c.

arrival.note: 4.24 ly ÷ 0.2c = 21.2 yr in the Earth/target frame, excluding launch acceleration and stellar motion. No braking.

name: Concept I: Laser sail (Starshot-class) — 0.046c capture
summary: Beyond-target · ultralight sailcraft, not a 1 kg probe. 0.046c cruise with conditional photogravitational capture at Alpha Cen A on the ~95 yr A/B arrival scale (Heller & Hippke 2017).
feasibility: Literature benchmark with extremely favorable sail loading (~0.00086 g/m²); the 95 yr A/B arrival is not a solved A-only parking orbit.
showstopper: A highly reflective, enormous ultralight sail must survive close stellar encounters. Launch, A-only full-stop geometry and orbit settling are not modeled.

arrival.note: Heller & Hippke (2017): ~95 yr A/B arrival scale. A-only capture and orbit settling require their own solution; this is not a simulated parking orbit. Proxima via A/B takes ~141 yr, not 95 yr.

name: Concept F: Chirped pellet slipstream
summary: Chirped pellet reflection: 3.75 kg of pellets supplies 300 km/s delta-v to a 2 kg probe; a conservative 5 AU speed budget gives solar v∞ 317.7 km/s with ~131 GJ ideal launch energy.
feasibility: TRL 2; ideal momentum transfer checks out, assuming fixed 100 km/s relative speed and 80% reflection efficiency.
showstopper: Pellet-stream aiming and ionisation over AU scales; one un-ionised pellet destroys the probe.

name: Concept E: Po-210 direct-charge ion drive
summary: Po-210 decay-powered xenon drive: 316.792 km/s rocket delta-v from 6.4 kg wet; radial equivalent impulse at 1 AU gives ideal solar v∞ 315.388 km/s.
feasibility: TRL 2–3; ideal decay energy and rocket equation check out, assuming 30% direct-charge conversion and 70% thruster efficiency.
showstopper: 0.4 kg Po-210 is about four times world output and decays about 0.5% per day; 30% direct-charge conversion is assumed versus only a few percent demonstrated.

name: Concept D: Moon-anchored photon-recycling cavity
summary: 280 km/s photon-recycling boost at 1 AU; ideal final v∞ 306.9 km/s using a 2 kg probe, ~392 MW for 714 s at ~40 g.
feasibility: TRL 2; ideal photon momentum checks out, but the moving laser cavity is unproven.
showstopper: Keep 300 effective reflections on a 22 m, 2.7 g/m² mirror receding at 280 km/s, with nanoradian pointing and wavelength/10 surface accuracy.

name: Concept G: Carbon sundiver sail at 3 solar radii
summary: Conditional carbon-based mirror: β = 0.7104 at 3 solar radii gives solar v∞ 300 km/s; ~646 m² sail, 1 kg probe, ~2.21 g peak radiation acceleration.
feasibility: TRL 2 conceptual study; energy and mass budgets close only with assumed 90% solar reflection and 0.5 g/m² distributed sail/support mass.
showstopper: No demonstrated sail combines these optics, thermal survival at 6.99 MW/m², deployment and control within ~1.323 kg total including a shielded probe. Bare graphene is mostly transparent.

name: Concept H: Distributed sundiver chip swarm
summary: 1,000 × 1 g chips with ~0.646 m² sails retain Concept G’s 300 km/s solar v∞; one representative flyby trajectory, ~4,237 yr to Proxima.
feasibility: TRL 2 conditional study; the same beta and total areal density preserve speed while dividing the probe and sail mass among independent chips.
showstopper: Unproven near-Sun mirror and millennia-long chip survival; no demonstrated chip braking, gathering or self-assembling ISRU factory. Splitting alone gives no speed gain.

name: Concept C (baseline): Tether network + STP Oberth
summary: 45 km/s inbound plunge, 24 km/s solar-thermal burn at 3.5 R_sun (v∞ 136.36 km/s) plus 15 speculative CNT tethers × 4 km/s; doc reference 196.36 km/s (6.55e-4 c).

name: Concept A (baseline): Chemical + Solar Oberth + tether chain
summary: 12 km/s chemical burn at 6 R_sun (v∞ 76.42 km/s) plus 12 speculative Zylon tethers × 3 km/s; doc reference 112.42 km/s (3.75e-4 c).

name: Concept B (baseline): Sundiver hybrid (chemical Oberth + solar sail)
summary: 6 km/s kick at 10 R_sun followed by a β = 0.25 radial sail; engine hybrid v∞ 107.56 km/s (3.59e-4 c).

name: Voyager 1 (baseline): Jupiter → Saturn
summary: Historical flyby sequence; illustrative unpowered patched-conic baseline calibrated to v∞ 16.9 km/s. See docs/analyses/voyager-baselines.md.

name: Voyager 2 (baseline): Jupiter → Saturn → Uranus → Neptune
summary: Historical flyby sequence; illustrative unpowered patched-conic baseline calibrated to v∞ 15.2 km/s. See docs/analyses/voyager-baselines.md.
